heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
**Turn a set of static Markdown spec files into a stable, addressable inventory of blocks, and say
exactly which blocks are new or changed since the last run.**

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
A block is a structural unit found by code: a paragraph, a list item, a table body row, or a fenced
code block. A block is **not** an atomic spec. Splitting blocks into claims is a language judgment and
belongs to atomization (F3, rel01 G2.2). F1 hands atomization its exact input: the pending blocks, with
source file, line range, heading path and verbatim text. F1 makes **no model calls**.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
Every spec is prose on disk before it is anything else (P-0: prose is the source of truth), so it is
always reviewable, diffable and versioned.

text:
- **Source selection:** a file is a spec source only if it matches `profile.spec_globs` and no

text: - **Segmentation** (deterministic, CommonMark parsing with source line maps):

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: | Heading | Not a block; updates `heading_path` |

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: | Paragraph | Block, kind `paragraph` |

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: | List item | Block per item, kind `list_item`. A sub-item is its own block with `parent_relation: nested`; a further paragraph or fence inside the same item keeps its own kind and gets `parent_relation: continuation` (D11) |

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: | Table | Block per **body row**, kind `table_row`, carrying the header row as `table_header` |

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: | Content inside a blockquote | Keeps its own kind, with `in_blockquote: true` |

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: | Fenced code | Block, kind `code`; pending only if `profile.include_code_blocks` is true |

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: | HTML comment, front matter, horizontal rule, blank lines | Skipped |

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **Hashing:** `text_hash` = SHA-256 of the block text after normalizing line endings to `\n`,
  trimming trailing whitespace per line, and collapsing runs of blank lines. Case, punctuation and
  inner whitespace are preserved.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: - **Identity on re-ingest of a file** (P-6), applied in order:

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: 1. same `text_hash` and same `heading_path` as an unmatched old live block → keep id, `unchanged`;

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
2. same `heading_path` and same ordinal position among blocks under that heading as an unmatched old
     live block → keep id, `changed`;

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
3. remaining new blocks → new id, `new`; remaining old blocks → `removed`: the record is kept with
     `removed_run` set, never deleted.
  `new · changed · unchanged · removed` is the **run's delta**. It is reported (CT-1.3 counts, the run
  output) and **not stored on the block** (D13): a stored per-run flag flips back on the next run.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **Pending set (D13), derived, never stored:** a block is pending when it is live (`removed_run` is
  null), it is not a `code` block unless `include_code_blocks` is true, and its `text_hash` differs from
  its `atomized_hash` (including when `atomized_hash` is null). A block therefore stays pending until
  the atomizer has actually processed its current text, however many runs that takes.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: - **Runs are atomic:**

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: - every store file is written to a temporary file and renamed only after the whole run succeeds;

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- a lock file in `.sdd/` serializes runs, and a second run waits up to **15 seconds**, then fails
    (D9);

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: - each successful run appends one line to `runs.jsonl`.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **Determinism:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, fixed key order, records sorted by id. Timestamps appear only in
  `runs.jsonl`. Identical sources and identical prior store give byte-identical
  `sources.jsonl` and `blocks.jsonl`.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **Failures are loud:** every error names the offending path or field and exits non-zero (CT-1.6). No
  store file changes on failure.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: **CT-1.1 — Block record** (`.sdd/blocks.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, sorted by `id`):

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
```json
{
  "id": "B-000123",
  "source": "sdd/specs/F1_ingest/spec.md",
  "kind": "paragraph | list_item | table_row | code",
  "heading_path": ["F1 — Ingest", "6. Acceptance criteria"],
  "lines": [42, 44],
  "text": "exact source text",
  "text_hash": "sha256:<hex>",
  "parent_block": "B-000120 | null",
  "parent_relation": "nested | continuation | null",
  "table_header": "string | null",
  "in_blockquote": false,
  "first_seen_run": "R-0007",
  "last_changed_run": "R-0009",
  "removed_run": "R-0011 | null",
  "atomized_hash": "sha256:<hex> | null"
}
```

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: Rules:

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: - `id` has the form `B-` plus 6 or more zero-padded digits, is assigned once, and is never reused.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: - `lines` are 1-based and inclusive.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: - `text` is the verbatim source slice of those lines.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- `parent_block` is non-null when a block belongs to a list item, and `parent_relation` says how
  (F1 D11): `nested` for a sub-item, `continuation` for a further paragraph or code fence inside the
  same item. Both are null otherwise, and they are always null or non-null together.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- `last_changed_run` is the run that first saw the current text. `removed_run` is set once, by the run
  that no longer found the block, and never cleared (D12).

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- `atomized_hash` is written **only by the atomizer** (F3 §4.5): the `text_hash` it last processed to
  completion. Ingest copies it unchanged. It is how pending is derived (D13).

text: **Segmentation**

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.1** *(block kinds and positions)* — **Given** a file with 3 paragraphs, a 2-item list and a
  table with a header and 2 body rows, **when** ingested, **then** exactly 7 blocks exist with kinds 3 ×
  `paragraph`, 2 × `list_item`, 2 × `table_row`, and correct `lines` and `heading_path`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.2** *(heading path)* — **Given** a paragraph under `## A` › `### B`, **when** ingested, **then**
  its `heading_path` is `["A", "B"]` and headings themselves produce no blocks. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.3** *(nested list)* — **Given** a list item containing a nested item, **when** ingested,
  **then** both are blocks and the nested one's `parent_block` is the outer one's id. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.4** *(table row carries header)* — **Given** a table, **when** ingested, **then** every body-row
  block has `table_header` equal to the header row text, and no block is created for the header or the
  delimiter row. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.5** *(blockquote)* — **Given** `> ⚠ Tokens must never be logged.`, **when** ingested, **then**
  one `paragraph` block exists with `in_blockquote: true`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.6** *(code blocks)* — **Given** a fenced code block and `include_code_blocks: false`, **when**
  ingested, **then** it is stored with kind `code` and is not in the pending set; **and with**
  `include_code_blocks: true` it is pending. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.30** *(a block belongs to its list item)* — **Given** a list item holding a second paragraph
  and a nested sub-item, **when** segmented, **then** the second paragraph is a `paragraph` block with
  `parent_block` naming the item and `parent_relation: continuation`, the sub-item is a `list_item`
  block with `parent_relation: nested`, and a top-level block has both fields null. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.7** *(skipped constructs)* — **Given** front matter, an HTML comment and a horizontal rule,
  **when** ingested, **then** none of them produces a block. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text: **Identity and change**

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.8** *(idempotent)* — **Given** an unchanged file ingested twice, **when** the second run
  completes, **then** it reports 0 new, 0 changed, 0 removed, and `blocks.jsonl` and `sources.jsonl`
  are byte-identical to the first run's. → *property.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.9** *(insertion keeps ids)* — **Given** a paragraph inserted above existing blocks, **when**
  re-ingested, **then** every pre-existing block keeps its id and the run classifies it `unchanged`,
  and only the inserted block is `new`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.10** *(edit keeps id)* — **Given** one word changed in a list item, **when** re-ingested,
  **then** that item keeps its id and the run classifies it `changed`, and no other block changes. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.11** *(removal is recorded)* — **Given** a paragraph deleted from a file, **when** re-ingested,
  **then** its record remains with `removed_run` set, and its id is never reused. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.31** *(pending until processed; D13)* — **Given** three blocks ingested and none atomized,
  **when** the unchanged file is ingested again, **then** all three are still pending (`new`); **given**
  the atomizer then records `atomized_hash` for one of them, **then** two are pending; **given** that
  block's text is then edited, **then** it is pending again as `changed`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **AC-1.12** *(normalization boundary)* — **Given** a block whose only change is trailing whitespace or
  CRLF line endings, **when** re-ingested, **then** it is `unchanged`; **given** a change of case
  ("must" → "MUST"), **then** it is `changed`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **D13 — The block record stores facts; the run's delta and the pending set are derived** (closes
  Q6, option c, 2026-09-18). `status` is removed from CT-1.1; `removed_run` and `atomized_hash` are
  added. *Why:* `status` meant "what the last ingest saw", but pending needs "has the atomizer processed
  this text". They diverge whenever a run ends early: after a call-cap exit (F3 AC-3.5), a block that
  failed its checks twice, or a crash, the next ingest would mark the unprocessed blocks `unchanged` and
  they would **silently never be atomized**. Deriving pending from `atomized_hash` removes that failure
  and makes AC-1.8 hold exactly as written. *Rejected:* (a) rewording AC-1.8 to a fixed point — leaves
  the silent drop in place for T10 to discover; (b) dropping `status` without saying how pending is
  derived. *Cost:* one CT-1.1 change, one F3 sentence, about six tests.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **D12 — ⚑ A `removed` record never matches again** (found while building T4). Re-adding deleted prose
  produces a **new** id. *Why:* "this id existed and was removed" should stay a fact; resurrecting an id
  would make the history ambiguous and would silently re-attach any later judgments made about the old
  block. *Cost:* re-adding a paragraph that was deleted by mistake costs its id, which is cheap —
  nothing downstream is lost, because a removed block has no nodes.

heading_path: F1 — Ingest: read static spec files into blocks
text:
- **D11 — A block records which list item it belongs to, and how** (closes Q5). `parent_relation` is
  `nested` for a sub-item and `continuation` for a further paragraph or fence inside one item.
  *Why:* a continuation paragraph genuinely belongs to its item, and losing that is a **silent** loss —
  atomized alone, "Model calls go through one interface with two backends" reads as a system-wide
  requirement and can be placed in the wrong family with nothing marking it as suspect. Measured on this
  repository: 3 of 649 list items are affected, so the cost of the fix is small and so is the blast
  radius of getting it wrong. *Rejected:* leaving it (a rare but silent mis-placement); merging an item
  and its continuations into one block — the item's lines are not contiguous when a sub-list sits
  between them, which would break the verbatim-slice property F3's span guard depends on.
  ⚠ Whether the atomizer *uses* the link as context is a separate decision, deliberately deferred to F3
  and measurable (G4 M4).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
**Define the one data contract every other part of the compiler reads and writes:** what a node is,
which properties it carries, how it is placed into exactly one layer and one family, how terms and
links are represented, and how status and conflicts are recorded.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: Nodes carry **abundant properties** (D8) for two jobs:

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - **placement** — layer and family, decided by code from recorded answers;

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - **retrieval** — finding related nodes (F5) without re-reading prose.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
Placement is deterministic code over answers produced by the atomizer (F3). This spec is testable
without any model call.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
**In scope:** node, term, link and conflict-record schemas · the hardcoded layer set · the placement
mapping rule · the family rule · component allocation · status derivation and precedence · id rules.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: **Non-goals**

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - ✗ Producing the answers placement consumes (atomization, Q-ATOM, Q-DESC) → F3.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - ✗ Where records are stored, views and queries → F4.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- ✗ Finding candidate related nodes → F5. Judging pairs and creating conflict records → F6, which in
  rel01 runs over the whole set and reports at the end (rel01 D26).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - ✗ Per-project layer meanings (P-7: meanings are fixed).

`requirement` · `constraint` · `assumption` · `verification` · `decision`.
Definitions become term-registry entries. Rationale and examples become annotations. Neither is a node.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: | `L1` Behavior | What an outside party observes, without naming protocol artefacts |

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
The set and meanings are constants in code. The profile may supply display names and section hints.
Hints are recorded as priors and never override an answer (P-7, P-12).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: Input: seven answers `Q1…Q7`, each `{answer: yes|no, quote: string|null}`, plus the node kind.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 1. `kind = verification` → `V`. The answers are ignored.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
2. Otherwise the layer is that of the **first `yes`** in order `Q1→C, Q2→L0, Q3→L1, Q4→L2, Q5→L3,
   Q6→L4, Q7→L5`.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
3. A later `yes` whose quote **overlaps** (shares at least one character offset with) an earlier `yes`
   quote is recorded and does not affect the layer.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
4. A later `yes` whose quote overlaps **no** earlier `yes` quote and maps to a **different** layer is a
   **T3 violation**. Placement returns `split_required` with both quotes, and no node is written.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 5. All `no` → layer `null`, ambiguity kind `unplaceable`.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
Quote overlap is computed on character offsets that code resolves in the source (F3 guard G2), never
on offsets supplied by the model.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
The primary term is chosen by the first rule that applies. ⚑ For a `V` node whose `verifies` resolved,
rule 3 is tried first (D18):

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 1. **Subject rule** — `canonical.subject` resolves to a term of kind `entity`, `data` or `event`.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
2. **Response rule** — the subject is an `actor`, a `component`, an `external_system` or "the system";
   the first `entity`/`data`/`event` term in `canonical.response`.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
3. **Verification rule** — a `V` node takes the family of the node(s) it verifies. If those differ, the
   node takes the first verified node's family and gets flag `family_disputed`.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
4. **Constraint rule** — a `C` node whose scope selects exactly one family belongs to it; otherwise to
   `(global)`.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 5. **Mention** (D17) — the first `entity`/`data`/`event` term the node uses in any role.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 6. **Component** (D19) — the subject is a `component` term: that term.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 7. **Fallback** — nothing resolves → family `null`, ambiguity kind `unresolved_term`.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
**Where `scope_selector` and `verifies` come from (D13).** Both are filled by code, never written by
the model directly:

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- `scope_selector` (a `C` node): `terms` = its resolved terms with role `scope`; `families` = those of
  kind `entity`, `data` or `event`; `categories` = those of kind `category`; `layers` = Q-DESC's closed
  answer `scope_layers` (any of `L0`…`L5`). An empty selector means the constraint is global.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- `verifies` (a `V` node): after every node of the run is formed, each node id or `AC-`/`CT-` label
  cited in the node's quotes or in Q-DESC's `verifies_text` resolves to the node(s) with that id or
  `label`, and each cited local label (`S4`, D20) to the nodes of the **same file** carrying it, when
  one block there carries it; each creates a `verifies` link with provenance `code`. Nothing cited → `verifies: []`, and the
  family falls to the subject rule or `unresolved_term`. The verification rule is then re-applied.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
`actor` and `category` terms never seed a family, and a `component` only by rule 6. A pin overrides the rule, and the node
gets flag `pinned_family`. Mentioning a term never makes a node a member of that term's family; it
creates a `uses_term` link.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - A node's `components` come from `allocated_to` links.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - An `L2` node stating ownership establishes the allocation for its family.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- Other nodes of that family are **proposed** for that component (flag `allocation_proposed`) until
  confirmed.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - `C` nodes are never allocated.

The facts stay in their own fields. The status is recomputed whenever a fact changes, so it cannot
disagree with them.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - `conflict_ids`: ids of graph-level conflict records (CT-2.4) this node belongs to.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - `related_conflict_nodes`: sorted union of all other members of those records.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
The two fields are consistent by construction: `related_conflict_nodes` is computed from the records,
never written independently.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: | Node | `N-000001`… · or an adopted human id (e.g. `AC-1.4`) | Assigned once, never reused. A human id found in the source is adopted if unique (P-12). A duplicate human id is a build error |

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: | Term | `term:<snake_case>` | Derived from the canonical name when created. Never renamed; renames become aliases |

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: | Conflict | `CF-000001` | Assigned once |

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: | Link | Key `(from, type, to)` | Unique per key |

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: Ids never embed family, layer or status (P-13 rule 3).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
A node is deleted when its source atom is gone: the block was removed, or re-atomization aligned it to
nothing. In one transaction:

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 1. delete the node record;

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 2. delete every link whose `from` or `to` is that node;

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
3. remove it from every conflict record's `members`; a record left with fewer than two members is
   `resolved` with reason `member_deleted`;

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 4. add a `stale_reasons` entry to every node that had a judged link to it;

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: 5. recompute statuses, the registry and the counts.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: Id counters are never rewound.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: Rules:

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- `scope_selector` is present only for `C` nodes, `verifies` only for `V` nodes, and `decision` only
  for `decision` nodes. Each is `null` otherwise.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- `keywords` are computed by code from `text` (lower-cased word tokens minus a fixed stop-word list,
  sorted, unique). They serve retrieval (F5) and are never model output.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - `status` always equals `derive_status` of the other fields (AC-2.14).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- `label` is the human id (`AC-<n>.<k>`, `CT-<n>.<k>`) of the block the node was formed from, on
  **every** node of that block, whether or not the id was adopted (D12). Null otherwise.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- `canonical.modality` is null only for an assumption, a decision or a verification stating no
  obligation, or together with ambiguity `missing_modality` (F3 D14).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: **Placement**

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.1** *(first yes wins)* — **Given** answers Q1 no, Q2 no, Q3 yes, Q6 yes with overlapping
  quotes, **when** placed, **then** layer is `L1`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.2** *(T3 violation)* — **Given** Q4 yes and Q5 yes with non-overlapping quotes, **when**
  placed, **then** the result is `split_required` carrying both quotes, and no node record is
  produced. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.3** *(all no)* — **Given** seven `no` answers for a requirement, **when** placed, **then** layer
  is `null` and `ambiguity` contains `unplaceable`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.4** *(verification bypass)* — **Given** kind `verification` with arbitrary answers, **when**
  placed, **then** layer is `V`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.5** *(order is fixed)* — **Given** every combination of yes/no over Q1–Q7 with mutually
  overlapping quotes, **when** placed, **then** the layer always equals the first yes in Q1→Q7 order.
  → *property.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: **Family**

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.6** *(subject rule)* — **Given** subject resolving to an `entity` term, **when** the family is
  derived, **then** family is that term and `family_rule` is `subject`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.7** *(response rule; actors never seed)* — **Given** subject "the system" and a response whose
  first entity term is `term:file`, with actor `term:owner` also present, **then** family is
  `term:file`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.8** *(verification rule)* — **Given** a `V` node verifying nodes in two different families,
  **then** it takes the first verified node's family and has flag `family_disputed`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.9** *(constraint rule)* — **Given** a `C` node whose scope selects one family, **then** it
  belongs to that family; **given** a scope spanning two families or a layer, **then** `(global)`. →
  *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.10** *(fallback and pin)* — **Given** no resolvable term, **then** family `null` with ambiguity
  `unresolved_term`; **given** a pin, **then** the pinned family, rule `pinned`, flag `pinned_family`.
  → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.11** *(mention is not membership)* — **Given** a node with family `term:share_link` whose terms
  include `term:file`, **then** a `uses_term` link to `term:file` exists and the family stays
  `term:share_link`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: **Status and conflicts**

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.12** *(precedence)* — **Given** a node with non-empty `conflict_ids` and non-empty `ambiguity`,
  **then** status is `conflict`; for every combination of the four facts, status follows
  conflict > ambiguous > stale > unchecked > validated. → *property.*

text:
- **AC-2.13** *(unchecked)* — **Given** a freshly placed node with `last_checked_run` null and no other
  facts, **then** status is `unchecked`, never `validated`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.14** *(status consistent)* — **Given** any node record, **when** validated against CT-2.1,
  **then** a stored `status` different from `derive_status` is rejected. → *contract.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.15** *(conflict membership consistent)* — **Given** open conflict records, **when**
  `related_conflict_nodes` is computed for a member, **then** it equals the sorted union of the other
  members of all its open records; a node in two records lists both `conflict_ids` (D14). → *property.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.23** *(deletion cascades)* — **Given** node A in an open conflict with B and linked to C,
  **when** A is deleted, **then** A's record and all links touching it are gone, the record is
  `resolved` with reason `member_deleted`, B is no longer `conflict`, and C has a `stale_reasons`
  entry. → *integration.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.16** *(resolution clears)* — **Given** a node whose only open conflict record becomes
  `resolved`, **when** facts are recomputed, **then** `conflict_ids` and `related_conflict_nodes` are
  empty and status is no longer `conflict`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.24** *(scope selector derived; D13)* — **Given** a `C` node whose scope-role terms are
  `term:upload` (entity) and `term:api` (category) and whose `scope_layers` is `[L3]`, **then**
  `scope_selector` is `{families: [term:upload], layers: [L3], terms: [term:api, term:upload],
  categories: [term:api]}` and its family is `term:upload` by the constraint rule. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.25** *(verifies resolved by citation; D13)* — **Given** a `V` node whose quote cites `AC-1.4`
  and two nodes labelled `AC-1.4` in family `term:table`, **then** `verifies` lists both, two
  `verifies` links with provenance `code` exist, and the family is `term:table` by the verification
  rule; **given** a `V` node citing nothing, **then** `verifies` is `[]`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.26** *(a criterion joins what it tests; D18)* — **Given** a `V` node whose subject term is the
  entity `term:node` and whose `verifies` resolves to a node in `term:candidate`, **then** its family is
  `term:candidate` by rule `verification`; **given** nothing resolved, **then** `term:node` by
  `subject`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.27** *(component as last resort; D19)* — **Given** a subject tagged `component`
  (`term:exhaustive_mode`) and no entity, data or event term anywhere, **then** the family is
  `term:exhaustive_mode`, rule `component`; **given** an entity in the response, **then** the response
  rule applies as before. → *unit.*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **AC-2.28** *(local labels; D20)* — **Given** a table row `| **S4 adjacent layer** | … |` in
  `f5.md`, a row labelled `S4` in `f9.md`, and a criterion in `f5.md` citing "S4", **then** the row's
  node carries `label: "S4"`, the criterion verifies only the `f5.md` node and joins its family; a local
  label carried by two blocks of one file resolves to nothing. → *unit.*

text:
- **D1 — Status is derived from facts, never stored independently** (implements D9/D15/D17).
  *Rejected:* setting status directly — status and facts would drift apart.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D2 — ⚑ One `status` field replaces the proposals' `draft_status` × `check_status`.** rel01 has a
  single writer and no drafting workflow. *Rejected for rel01:* two status axes.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D3 — Removed nodes are deleted, not kept** (owner decision, rel01 D24). When a node's source text
  is gone, its record, its links and its membership in conflict records are deleted in the same
  transaction. *Why deletion is safe:* `.sdd/` is committed to git, so history lives in git rather than
  in a graveyard of `removed` records, and every query, count and view stops having to filter them out.
  *What deletion costs, and how it is covered:*

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **Id reuse.** Ids must still never be reused, so `graph.meta.json` keeps monotonic **id counters**
    (F4 CT-4.1). A deleted id is never issued again (AC-2.20).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **Dangling references.** Deleting a node deletes every link touching it, drops it from every
    conflict record, and closes a record that falls below two members (§4.9).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **Neighbours.** Every node that had a judged link to the deleted node gains a `stale_reasons` entry,
    so it is re-checked rather than silently keeping a verdict about something gone.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- ⚠ **Asymmetry with F1:** F1 keeps *blocks* with `removed_run` set (F1 D13), because block identity drives
    change detection across runs. Only *nodes* are deleted. Say so if this should change too.

text:
- **D4 — ⚑ `keywords` computed by code** as a cheap retrieval signal for F5. *Rejected:* model-generated
  keywords — non-deterministic and unverifiable.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D5 — ⚑ Conflict kinds** `contradiction · duplication · subsumption · ambiguity` (from the pre-rel01

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status

- **D6 — ⚑ A `V` node verifying nodes in several families** takes the first verified node's family and

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D7 — ⚑ New link type `decides`** from a decision node to the nodes it changed (P-12 "links to the
  nodes it changed").

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text: - **D8 — ⚑ Modality set** adds `SHOULD NOT` to the proposals' list.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D9 — ⚑ The family rules apply literally in order** (found while building T9). §4.4 says "the first
  rule that applies", so a `C` or `V` node whose subject is an entity takes that entity's family by the
  subject rule before the constraint or verification rule is reached. *Why:* it is what the text says,
  and it keeps "uploaded files must never exceed 5 GB" in the `file` family, where a reader looks for it.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D10 — ⚑ Which human ids are adopted** (found while building T9). Only `AC-<n>.<k>` and `CT-<n>.<k>`,
  which are unique across the repository by construction; only as the **label** at the start of a
  paragraph or list item (a mention or a table row is not the claim); and only when the block forms
  exactly one node. *Why:* `D<n>`, `Q<n>` and `T<n>` are unique only inside one spec (constitution §1),
  so adopting them would fail every multi-spec build on the duplicate rule. See Q4 for the multi-atom
  case.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D12 — Every node formed from a labelled block carries the label** (closes Q4, option c). A block
  that forms exactly one node still adopts its human id (AC-2.19); a block that forms several gives
  them `N-` ids, and all of them carry `label: "AC-1.8"`. *Why:* in two live runs, 13–14 of 18 F1
  acceptance criteria formed several nodes, so without the field the id survived only inside the
  text. *Rejected:* (a) text only — "which nodes came from AC-1.8" would need a text search; (b)
  suffixed ids (`AC-1.8.1`) — a new id form and a constitution change for what a field does.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D13 — Code fills `scope_selector` and `verifies` from answers already given** (closes Q3, option b;
  §4.4). *Why:* both fields feed placement (family rules 3, 4) and retrieval (F5 S3), and nothing
  produced them; the atomizer already tags scope terms, and the `label` field (D12) makes a cited
  criterion resolvable by lookup. One closed Q-DESC field (`scope_layers`) is the only new model output.
  *Rejected for rel01:* (a) leaving them empty — S3 and rule 4 would be dead code in production.
  *Deferred past rel01 (rel01 D31):* (c) `verifies` and `constrains` as Q-PAIR relations, which would
  find targets that are described but not named, at the cost of model calls and an ordering loop
  (family → retrieval → judgment → family).

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D14 — ⚑ A conflict record resolved by a deletion keeps its members** (found while building T11).
  §4.9 step 3 says to remove the deleted node from `members`, but CT-2.4 requires at least two. A record
  falling below two is resolved (`member_deleted`) and keeps its member list as history; an **open**
  record never lists a deleted node, and the store checks only open records' members.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D15 — Ambiguity kind `mixed_layers`** (F3 D23): a node whose layer answers still point at two
  layers after the split re-ask is placed by the first yes and carries this ambiguity, quoting the
  second yes.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D16 — A term may record the term it is a kind of (`broader`)** (rel01 D33 R1, F3 D25). "Review
  item" is narrower than "item": both stay terms with their own families, and the relation is kept for
  later views rather than lost in a merge.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D17 — A mentioned entity names the family before null** (rel01 D32 R4). Rule 5 takes the first
  `entity`/`data`/`event` term the node uses in any role. *Why:* 20 of 84 gate nodes had no family,
  10 of them because no subject term was tagged. *Narrows* the principle "mentioning a term never makes
  a node a member" to: never while any earlier rule applies. AC-2.11 still holds.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D18 — ⚑ A verification that resolved `verifies` takes that family first** (M3 gate review, I-56;
  owner approved the direction 2026-09-19). *Amends D9 for `V` nodes.* On R12, nine of F5's criteria
  sat in `term:node` because "Given two nodes…" gave the subject; the Given clause names a criterion's
  fixture, not what it tests. D9's reason (a `C` node about files stays in `file`) does not transfer,
  because a criterion's subject is its setup.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D19 — ⚑ A `component` subject names the family as a last resort**, after mention and before null
  (M3 gate review, I-56). "Exhaustive mode" had about five claims and no family, because components never
  seeded one. Placed last, it takes only nodes that would otherwise be null. Actors and categories
  still never seed a family.

heading_path: F2 — Node & layer model: nodes, layers, families, terms, links, status
text:
- **D20 — ⚑ Local labels** (M3 gate review, I-56). A table row that opens with an id (`S1`, `T1`, bold

  every multi-spec build (D10).

**Turn each pending block into atomic nodes that conform to F2.** Haiku answers small, closed,
schema-bound questions. Code checks every answer before accepting it, records it, and does
everything else: offsets, quantities, placement and identity.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - Each question has a versioned schema, e.g. `q-atom/1`.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 1. Validate each answer as soon as it arrives, before any dependent question is asked.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 2. On failure, re-ask **once**, including the specific failed check in the question.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 3. On a second failure, **no node is created**:

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - the block is recorded as `atomize_failed` with the failed check;

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - the block stays pending;

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - an item is added to the review queue.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
4. **Batching (rel01 D30).** Q-ATOM may carry several blocks in one call. Each block's answer is
   validated on its own; a failure re-asks **only that block**, alone, once. One block failing never
   discards another block's accepted answer.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards

Words, order, case and

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **Placement T3** (F2 AC-2.2) returning `split_required` counts as a Q-ATOM failure for that block:
  re-ask Q-ATOM once with both quotes. If the re-asked atoms still require a split, the node is formed
  with the first yes's layer and ambiguity `mixed_layers` (D23) — the block does not fail.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **Quantities** are parsed from the quotes by code into a value and unit. They are normalized for
  time (to seconds), size (to bytes; KB = 1000, KiB = 1024) and count/percent (unchanged). A quantity
  the parser cannot read adds ambiguity `unbounded_quantity`.
  ⚑ Months and years are recorded with `normalized: null` (D12). A count is recognized only after a
  bounding word ("at most 3 times"); numbers inside identifiers, dates and versions are not
  quantities.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: For each validated atom:

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 1. Resolve term tags against the registry. Exact names and aliases resolve directly.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 2. Otherwise ask Q-TERM:

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - `different` → create a `proposed` term;

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- `same` → the name becomes an alias of that existing term, and a `term_same` review item lets a
     person reject the merge (D20);

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - `narrower` → a `proposed` term of its own, recording `broader` (D25); no review item;

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- `unsure` → a `proposed` term, a `term_unsure` review item, and ambiguity `pending_review` on the
     node until reviewed (D16).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 3. Compute quantities, `keywords`, spans and lines.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 4. Call F2 placement (layer, family, components).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 5. Create `uses_term` links (provenance `code`).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 6. Set `last_checked_run: null`. Status derives to `unchecked` or `ambiguous` (F2).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 7. Write through F4 atomically per block: either all nodes from a block are written, or none.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
8. In the same write, set the block's `atomized_hash` to its current `text_hash` (F1 D13). This is
   what takes a block out of the pending set, so it is set **only** when the block completed: a block
   that failed its checks, hit the call cap, or was interrupted keeps its old value and stays pending.
   A block yielding zero atoms (all sentences non-normative) still completes.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: When a `changed` block is re-atomized, new atoms are aligned to the block's existing active nodes:

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 1. by span overlap of quotes on the new block text with the old nodes' `text`;

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: 2. then by equal `canonical.subject` and `canonical.response`.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: | `unchanged` | Same id; record untouched except `source.lines` |

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: | `edited` | Same id; fields replaced; every judged link touching it gains a `stale_reasons` entry |

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: | `split` | Old id kept by the best-overlapping atom; others get new ids |

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: | `merged` | Best-overlapping old id kept; other old nodes deleted (F2 §4.9) |

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: | `new` | New id |

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: | `removed` | Old node deleted (F2 §4.9) |

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - A `removed` block deletes all its nodes.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- Alignments are applied automatically, recorded with `confirmed: auto`, and listed in the run report
  (⚑ D3).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards

  question's instructions + canonical JSON input)` per item (D21). A lock hit **replays** the stored
  answer through the same guards, with no model call; if a guard now rejects it, the item is asked.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - `sddc compile --no-replay` forces asking.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:

text: - Pending blocks are processed in `(source path, first line)` order, so a run is reproducible.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards

text:
- In rel01 the checks (F5 retrieval, F6 judgment) run as a **separate phase after atomization**
  (F6 §4.1), not per node, so every node is visible to every pair.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards

text:
- The pipeline keeps a per-node extension point `on_node_formed(node)`, unused in rel01. It is where
  live editing would hook checking back into atomization. ⚠ Not a Claude Code hook: rel01 has none.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
4.8 Order of processing, and where the checks run
text:
- **The run never stops at a conflict** (rel01 D26). Every conflict found is recorded on the nodes and
  in the graph's conflict records, and the run continues to the last pending block.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards

text:
- The run ends with one report (§4.10): blocks processed, nodes formed, **blocks that completed and
  formed no node, with the roles their sentences were given** (D33), model calls and usage, every
  conflict found, and every attention item opened.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: **Backend**

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.1** *(child environment)* — **Given** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the parent environment and
  `pass_api_key: false`, **when** the `claude-code` backend spawns a call, **then** the child
  environment has `SDD_COMPILER_CHILD=1` and no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and the command line contains
  `-p`, `--model haiku`, `--output-format json`, `--json-schema`, and not `--bare`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.2** *(.env confined)* — **Given** a `.env` with keys, **when** the `claude-code` backend runs,
  **then** `.env` is never read; **when** the `anthropic-api` backend runs, **then** the key is read from
  `.env`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.3** *(usage recorded)* — **Given** a fake response carrying usage and cost, **when** accepted,
  **then** the judgment record contains them, plus the backend, model and CLI version. → *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.4** *(backend unavailable)* — **Given** `claude` not on PATH, **when** `atomize` runs, **then**
  it exits `6` and no store file changes. → *integration.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.5** *(call cap)* — **Given** `max_calls_per_run: 2` and three pending blocks needing calls,
  **then** the run exits `5`, completed blocks are written, and the rest stay pending. → *integration.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: **Guards and re-ask**

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.6** *(G2 re-ask then fail)* — **Given** a fake Q-ATOM answer quoting text absent from the
  block, twice, **then** the question is asked exactly twice, the second time including the failed
  check; no node is written; the block stays pending; an `atomize_failed` review item exists. →
  *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.7** *(G2 offsets by code)* — **Given** a quote occurring twice in the block and two atoms
  quoting it, **then** they anchor to the first and second occurrences respectively. → *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.8** *(G3 coverage)* — **Given** a block with two "must" sentences and an answer covering one,
  **then** a re-ask occurs naming the uncovered sentence. → *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.9** *(G4 injection)* — **Given** canonical fields containing "AES-256" absent from the quotes,

  `inferred_node` review item. → *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text: - **AC-3.10** *(G5 schema)* — **Given** an answer missing `atoms`, **then** a re-ask occurs. → *unit.*

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **AC-3.11** *(G6 weak words)* — **Given** "uploads must be fast" and `fast` in `weak_words`, **then**

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards

- **AC-3.12** *(T3 split re-ask)* — **Given** Q-DESC answers producing `split_required`, **then** Q-ATOM

text:
- **D9 — G2 matches quotes *up to layout*** (closes Q4, 2026-09-18, option a). Runs of whitespace, and
  the `>` markers Markdown repeats on wrapped blockquote lines, may differ between a quote and the
  source; words, order, case and punctuation may not, and anchors stay true source offsets.
  *Why:* strict matching rejected 5 of 20 real blocks whose quotes were correct prose, and the re-asks
  made batching dearer than one call per block; with D9 the same blocks gave 0 failures (rel01 S20).
  *Rejected:* (b) strict matching after re-wrapping quotes in code — the same rule, stated less
  directly.
  *Extended 2026-09-18 (T9, ⚑ under the same principle):* `*` emphasis marks are also layout. Haiku
  quotes `**Given** a file` as `Given a file`; strict matching failed **14 of 20** acceptance-criterion
  blocks, and ignoring `*` brought that to 0 (rel01 S22).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D10 — ⚑ Extended thinking is off by default** (found while building T8; profile
  `atomizer.thinking`). Claude Code thinks by default. On one Q-DESC call, thinking was 2,896 of 3,588
  output tokens and took the call from ≈ 5 s to 25–35 s; batches of 8 atoms exceeded the 120 s timeout.
  The questions are small and closed. On the one atom compared, the answer without thinking placed the
  claim correctly (L1) and the thinking answer did not (C). One sample; the M2 gate measures quality.
  *Mechanism:* `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` in the child environment. ⚠ Every cost figure before rel01
  S21 was measured with thinking on.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D11 — ⚑ `vague_term` comes from G6 only** (found while building T8). Offered `vague_term`, Haiku

  `missing_actor`, `referential` and `scope`.

text:
- **D12 — ⚑ Months and years are not normalized.** Neither has a fixed length; converting one would
  invent a number. The raw value and unit are kept.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D13 — G4 grounds against the atom's block and its heading path** (closes Q5, option a).
  `inferred` means "not in the source at all". *Why:* read narrowly (the atom's own quotes), G4 flagged
  8 of 17 real atoms, all context resolution ("here" → "F1" from the heading); read widely, 1 of 20, and
  that one real (rel01 S21). *Rejected:* (b) narrow — ≈ 8 false review items per 17 atoms.
  *Accepted cost:* borrowing a value from a neighbouring claim in the same block is not flagged.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D14 — A requirement or constraint without a modality is formed and flagged** (closes Q6, option b).
  `canonical.modality` is null and the node carries ambiguity `missing_modality` (F2 CT-2.1), so its
  status derives to `ambiguous`. *Why:* failing it removed its whole block (AC-3.16) for a claim that is
  merely under-specified; defaulting to `MUST` (option c) would invent an obligation strength the
  author did not write.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D15 — ⚑ `source.spans` are offsets into the block's text** (found while building T10). The block's
  verbatim text is stored with the block (F1 CT-1.1), so block id plus span is a complete address and
  no node needs the file to be located. Multi-span text is joined with ` … `.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D16 — ⚑ A `same`/`unsure` Q-TERM verdict keeps the new term separate until reviewed** (T10): the
  node links the new `proposed` term and carries `pending_review`; accepting the review item merges it
  as an alias. *Why:* merging on the model's word alone would move nodes between families unreviewed.
  *Narrowed by D20:* applies to `unsure` only.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D17 — ⚑ Q-TERM is asked only when similar names exist** (T10). "Similar" = a shared word (plural
  folded) or a `difflib` ratio ≥ 0.8, at most 10 candidates (Q3's default). With no candidate the
  answer could only be `different`, so no call is made; on a first run most terms need none.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D18 — ⚑ Pending blocks are processed in chunks of 20** (T10). One chunk runs every model step
  (Q-ATOM, Q-DESC, the split re-ask, Q-TERM) before any of it is kept, so a call-cap stop keeps the
  finished chunks and leaves the interrupted one pending, whole (AC-3.5).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D19 — ⚑ Term hygiene** (T10). A family is a term, so a term must name a thing. On 32 live blocks
  Haiku tagged 142 terms for 49 nodes, 119 used once — ids (`AC-1.9`, `D9`), values (`120 s timeout`),
  settings with values, clauses — making families near one per node (rel01 S23). Code drops a tag with
  a digit, a `:`/`=`, or more than four words, and folds names to the singular before matching; the
  Q-DESC prompt defines a term as a short singular noun phrase naming a thing.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D20 — A Q-TERM `same` verdict merges at once, and a person may undo it** (closes Q7, option b).
  The new name becomes an alias of the existing term, all its tags resolve there, and a `term_same`
  item records the merge; rejecting it splits the name back out. No node becomes `ambiguous` for it.
  *Why:* on 32 live blocks 7 of 8 verdicts were `same` and all plausible, yet under D16 they made 16 of
  49 nodes `ambiguous` (rel01 S23). *Rejected:* (a) D16 for every verdict — a flood of ambiguity over
  merges that were right. `unsure` keeps D16.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D21 — ⚑ The judgment lock is per item, and its key includes the instructions** (T12). Q-ATOM,
  Q-DESC and Q-TERM are batched (rel01 D30); keyed per call, editing one block would change its
  20-block batch and re-ask all twenty. Keyed per item — by the item's content, not its id — only the
  changed item is asked, and a moved block keeps its answer. A call's usage is stored once
  (`batch_of`, CT-3.2) so costs are never counted twice. The instructions are in the key so that a
  prompt change re-asks instead of replaying answers to a different prompt. A re-ask carrying a note
  (the T3 split, AC-3.12) is never answered from the lock; the latest record for a key wins.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D22 — ⚑ Alignment measures text overlap, and an aligned id beats an adopted one** (T12). §4.6's
  "span overlap" is computed as a `difflib` ratio (≥ 0.5) between the old node's `text` and the new
  atom's text, because the old block's text is gone once ingest replaces it. Ties break by old id,
  then atom order. When a labelled block's atom aligns to an old `N-` node, the old id is kept (the
  `label` still names the criterion): identity across edits outranks adoption (F2 AC-2.19). An
  `unchanged` node keeps its whole record — check state included — except its `source`.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D23 — A split the model refuses twice is formed, flagged `mixed_layers`** (owner, 2026-09-18,
  closing I-42). *Why:* on `vision.md`, 4 of 31 blocks failed every run, all a bold title plus its
  explanation: title and body answered different layer questions with non-overlapping quotes, and the
  model rightly kept one claim. Failing them cost a re-ask on every compile and left them out of the
  graph. Two refusals are evidence of one claim, so the node takes the first yes's layer and the
  ambiguity names the second (F2 D15). *Rejected:* special-casing bold lead-ins — narrower, and the same
  refusal appears on Given/When/Then criteria (I-22, I-30).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D24 — A backend failure mid-run keeps finished work** (owner, 2026-09-18, closing I-43). Exit `6`
  now behaves like exit `5`: finished chunks and their judgment-lock records are written; the
  interrupted chunk stays pending. *Why:* a usage limit (hit twice in live runs) would otherwise
  discard every paid-for answer of the run.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D9 extended (rel01 D32 R5, R10):** backticks are layout, like `*`; a case difference in a quote's
  first letter only is tolerated ("a Q-TERM…" for "A Q-TERM…" failed a block in both gate runs).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D25 — Q-TERM `narrower`** (rel01 D33 R1). A kind of a candidate keeps its own term and family and
  records `broader` (F2 D16). `same` is defined as synonyms, spellings and plurals, with examples.
  *Why:* at the M2 gate 9 of 16 `same` verdicts explained themselves as "a specialized form of".

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D26 — Q-DESC is shown the vocabulary** (rel01 D33 R2): up to 100 existing term names — the chunk's
  own files' terms first, then the most used — to reuse when they name the same thing, with the rule "a
  kind of X is not X". The list is rendered outside the instructions, so it is **not** in the lock key
  (D21). *Why:* 72–79 % of gate terms were used once, so families held one node each.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D27 — Prompt corrections from the M2 gate** (rel01 D32 R3, R9, R11). Q1 asks about meaning, not
  words such as "every" or "never"; Q3 asks whether an outsider can check the claim without looking
  inside the system; Q-ATOM lists what is *not* a claim (titles, status and process notes, open
  questions, pointers, legends, tier tags, and every sentence after *Why:* or *Rejected:*).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D28 — An acceptance criterion is one verification atom** (rel01 D32 R8). A block labelled `AC-…` is
  folded by code into a single `verification` atom holding all its quotes; the prompt says the same for
  Given/When/Then text. *Why:* at the gate, criteria became Given/When/Then fragments plus a stray atom
  from the tier tag. A side effect: such blocks form one node, so they adopt their `AC-` id (F2
  AC-2.19).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D29 — Canonical subject and response must say something** (rel01 D32 R7): an empty or blank one fails
  G5 and is re-asked. *Why:* two gate nodes were formed with both empty.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D30 — Resolve a reference before flagging it** (owner, after R6: R13). Q-DESC is told to resolve
  "it", "this", "they" from the same block or its section and to write the resolved thing as the
  subject; `referential` is flagged only when neither names it. *Why:* after R1 … R11, `referential` was
  still on about a third of nodes and the main cause of `ambiguous`.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D31 — `narrower` points from the specific to the general** (owner, after R6: R14). The Q-TERM prompt
  says so, with a reversed example, and code refuses a `narrower` verdict whose candidate already
  contains every word of the new term ("backend" against "claude code backend"): the new term is the
  broader one, so the answer is re-asked. *Why:* about 1 in 4 `narrower` verdicts in R6 were reversed.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D32 — ⚑ `definition` is only for what a word means** (M3 gate review, I-56). Q-ATOM labelled all
  seven of F5's candidate-source table rows `definition` and formed no node, so F5's core rules were
  absent from the graph with no warning. The prompt now says that a row or item stating how something
  behaves, is decided or is checked is a claim, with F5's S1 row as the example. ⚠ **Still open:** F2 §4.1
  says "definitions become term-registry entries", but nothing writes them (`defined_by` is always
  null). A sentence labelled `definition` is dropped silently. This is the I-26 pattern again: a field
  with readers and no producer (build-plan I-59).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D33 — ⚑ The report counts blocks that formed no node** (M3 gate review, I-59). A block whose
  sentences are all `definition`, `context` or `rationale` is completed, correctly, and forms nothing;
  until now the run said "65 of 65 completed" while seven of F5's rules vanished. The summary carries
  `empty_blocks` and, per block, its file, lines and sentence roles. *Not* an attention item (§4.9):
  most empty blocks are headings and legends, and a queue of them would bury the real items. ⚠ The
  other half of I-59 — a producer for `definition` sentences (F2 §4.1) — is still open.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D34 — ⚑ A table row is one claim, enforced in code** (R15, I-64). With D32 the rows became
  claims, and F5's `S3` row came back as one atom per cell: "A `C` node whose `scope_selector` covers
  the other node", "by the rule of D9", "the selector that matched" — one rule as three fragment nodes
  in three families. A row's cells are the parts of one rule, so `one_criterion` now folds a row's
  atoms into one, keeping every quote in row order, as it already did for `AC-` blocks (D28). The
  prompt says the same, and adds the rule Q-DESC has had since I-15: **the "section" and "table header"
  lines are context and are never quoted** (R15, I-63: 4 of 66 blocks failed on exactly that).

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D35 — ⚑ An annotation that cannot be located is dropped and reported, never raised** (R16, I-67).
  Rationale and example sentences become annotations (F2 §4.1), and their quotes were located by the
  same guard that anchors atoms — which *raises*. Q-ATOM merged two source sentences into one
  `rationale` quote, and the exception escaped at node-forming time, **after every model call of the
  run had been paid for**, losing the whole compile. An annotation carries no claim, so an unlocatable
  one is dropped and listed in the run report (`annotations_dropped`), beside D33's empty blocks.
  ⚠ **Open (build-plan I-68):** F3 D24 keeps finished work only for the two *expected* stops, exit `5`
  and `6`. An unexpected exception anywhere after the first call still discards the run and its lock
  records. The exit code for an internal error is not specified (CT-1.6 has none), so this is the
  owner's call.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D36 — ⚑ A block that is one claim by its own form is never asked to split** (R16, I-70). D34 folds
  a table row's atoms into one, and D28 does the same for an `AC-` block — and then AC-3.12's split
  re-ask asked the model to separate the row's rule from its evidence cell, and it obliged: all seven
  of F5's source rows became two nodes, one of them a bare fragment. Such a block now takes D23's
  path directly — placed by its first yes, flagged `mixed_layers` — decided in the first pass, so it
  also saves a model call. AC-3.12 still governs every other block.

heading_path: F3 — Atomizer: pending blocks → nodes, with Haiku and deterministic guards
text:
- **D37 — ⚑ An unusable answer is rejected, not fatal** (C, the dogfood run: I-79). A Q-ATOM call
  over 20 dense spec blocks returned no `structured_output`, and the backend raised it as "the model
  backend is unavailable" (exit `6`), ending a 173-block compile after 19 blocks. One call producing
  nothing usable is the same event as an answer failing a guard: `AnswerRejected` now travels to the
  batch layer, which re-asks **each item alone** — a far smaller prompt, and usually enough. A dead
  backend, a missing binary and a 429 stay exit `6`. *Why it matters at scale:* on 733 blocks, one
  unlucky call in fifty would otherwise stop every long compile.

- **AC-4.1** *(sharding)* — **Given** nodes in families `term:a`, `(global)` and `null`, **when**
  written, **then** they are in `nodes/a.jsonl`, `nodes/_global.jsonl` and `nodes/_unplaced.jsonl`.

  the transaction commits, **then** it appears only in `nodes/b.jsonl`, and its outgoing links move to
  `edges/b.jsonl`. → *unit.*
