heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
> **Spec-ID:** F5 · **Status:** 🟢 approved · **Drafted:** 2026-09-17 · **Approved:** 2026-09-18 (rel01 D28)
> ⛔ **Coding gated (rel01 D20).**
> **Source:** rel01 sub-goal G3.1 · approved proposal P-10 and the candidate rule in
> [`../../design/rel01_design/core-working-principle.md`](../../design/rel01_design/core-working-principle.md)
> §5–§6 · rel01 D26 (batch) · the F5 conflict list of 2026-09-16 (items 5.1–5.5).
> **Depends on:** F2 (node properties) · F4 (indexes). **Feeds:** F6 (pair judgment).
> **⚑ Drafting choices** are marked in §7.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
**For every node that needs checking, produce a small, ranked, explained set of other nodes worth
comparing it against — deterministically, with no model call.**

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
Judging every pair is quadratic and unaffordable: 500 nodes is 124,750 pairs, one Haiku call each.
Retrieval is what makes checking affordable, and it is also the **main risk in the whole design**: a
pair never proposed is a relation never found. So every candidate carries *why* it was proposed, the
counts are recorded, and an exhaustive mode exists to measure what the ranked mode misses.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
**In scope:** candidate sources · deterministic scoring and capping · the pair key that makes a pair
identifiable across runs · which nodes need checking in a run · the exhaustive mode used for
measurement · `sddc pairs`.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: **Non-goals**

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: - ✗ Judging a pair, or deciding what a relation means → F6.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: - ✗ Embeddings or any learned similarity (rel01: deterministic only; vision O2).

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: - ✗ Context packs for code generation → F7 design note.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | T1 | `sddc compile` reaches the check phase | `sdd_compiler.retrieval::candidates_for` |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | T2 | A person inspects what would be judged, or measures coverage | `sddc pairs [--node ID] [--exhaustive] [--json]` |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
4.1 Which nodes are checked in a run
text:
A node needs checking when its `status` is `unchecked`, or `stale`, or when it is `ambiguous` and was
never judged. Nodes whose text and whose candidates are unchanged since their `last_checked_run` are
skipped: their verdicts are replayed from the judgment lock (F3 §4.7).

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
4.1 Which nodes are checked in a run
text: Checking order is `(source file, first line, node id)`, so a run is reproducible.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: For node **A**, candidates are gathered from these sources. Each source records the evidence it used.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S1 same family** | Same `family` (not `(global)`) | family id |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S2 shared subject term** | Shares a term of kind `entity`, `data` or `event`, **or one that is a kind of the other** (`broader`, D11) | the term ids, and the chain that matched |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S3 constraint scope** | A `C` node whose `scope_selector` covers the other node, in either direction, by the rule of D9 | the selector that matched |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S4 adjacent layer** | Same family and layer distance ≤ 1 in the order L0…L5 | both layers |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S5 shared keywords** | At least `min_shared_keywords` (default 2) common `keywords` | the shared keywords |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S6 same measured property** | Both carry a quantity of the same dimension (time, size, count, percent), in claims sharing a term **or a keyword** (D11) | the dimension and both values |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S7 same source block** | Both atomized from the same block | the block id |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: | **S8 two kinds of one thing** | Their terms are not shared, and neither is above the other, but both are kinds of one term (`broader`, D12) | the shared parent and both terms |

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
**Why S5 and S6 exist (⚑ D1).** The pre-rel01 rule was family, shared term, constraint scope and
adjacent layer only. That never proposes the first node of a family, and it misses conflicts whose
nodes share no term — the "SQLite versus 100 concurrent writes" shape. S5 catches wording overlap
without embeddings; S6 catches two numbers about the same thing, which is the most common real
contradiction.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
```text
score = 3.0 · S1 + 2.0 · S2(per shared term, max 4.0) + 2.0 · S3 + 1.0 · S4
      + 0.5 · S5(per shared keyword, max 2.0) + 2.5 · S6 + 1.5 · S7 + 1.0 · S8
```

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: - Candidates below `min_score` (default 1.0) are dropped.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- The rest are ranked by score, then by node id, and the top `max_pairs_per_node` (default 6, D13) are
  returned.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- Both numbers live in the profile (CT-5.2). They are **starting values to tune with measurement**, not
  findings.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
A pair is unordered. Its key is
`pair_key = sha256(min(id_a, id_b) + "|" + max(id_a, id_b) + "|" + text_hash of each, in the same order)`.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
The key changes when either node's text changes, which is exactly when the pair must be judged again.
F6 uses it for the judgment lock, and F5 uses it to drop pairs already judged in this run.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
`sddc pairs --exhaustive` returns **all** pairs among the checked nodes, with their scores, without
judging anything. It exists so the ranked mode can be measured against it on a labelled corpus: of the
true relations found exhaustively, how many did ranking propose? That measurement belongs to G4; this
spec only guarantees the mode exists and is deterministic.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: Compilation never uses exhaustive mode: it is an offline measurement tool.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
Per run, for later measurement (G4): nodes checked, candidates proposed, pairs after the cap, pairs
dropped by `min_score`, pairs dropped by the cap, pairs replayed from the lock. These go into the run
record (F1 CT-1.3, extended by CT-5.3).

text: **CT-5.1 — Candidate**

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging

```json
  "evidence": [ {"source": "S2", "detail": {"terms": ["term:share_link"]}, "points": 2.0 },
                {"source": "S6", "detail": {"dimension": "time", "values": ["30 d", "1 h"]}, "points": 2.5 } ],
  "rank": 1 }
```

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: `evidence` is never empty, and its `points` sum to `score`.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: **Sources**

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.1** *(same family)* — **Given** two nodes in family `term:share_link`, **then** each is a
  candidate for the other with S1 evidence. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.2** *(shared subject term, actors excluded)* — **Given** two nodes sharing `term:file` (an
  entity) and two others sharing only `term:owner` (an actor), **then** the first pair is proposed with
  S2 evidence and the second is not proposed by S2. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.3** *(constraint scope; amended by D9)* — **Given** a `C` node scoped to category
  `term:endpoint` in layer `L3` and an `L3` node using `term:endpoint`, **then** the pair is proposed
  with S3 evidence naming the selector; **given** a `C` node scoped to `L3` only and an `L3` node sharing
  no term or keyword with it, **then** S3 does not contribute. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.4** *(adjacent layer)* — **Given** two nodes of one family in `L1` and `L2`, **then** S4
  contributes; **given** `L1` and `L4`, **then** S4 does not. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.5** *(shared keywords)* — **Given** two nodes sharing 2 keywords and `min_shared_keywords: 2`,
  **then** S5 contributes and names the shared keywords; **given** one shared keyword, **then** S5 does
  not. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.6** *(same measured property; amended by D11)* — **Given** two nodes sharing
  `term:share_link`, one with "30 days" and one with "1 hour", **then** S6 contributes with dimension
  `time` and both values; **given** two nodes with no shared term but a shared keyword, one "5 GB" and
  one "5 GiB", **then** S6 contributes; **given** no shared term and no shared keyword, **then** it does
  not. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.7** *(same block)* — **Given** two nodes atomized from one block, **then** S7 contributes. →
  *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.17** *(two kinds of one thing; D12)* — **Given** nodes whose terms are `term:export_archive`
  and `term:workspace_export`, both recorded `broader: term:export`, **then** S8 contributes naming the
  shared parent, and S2 does not; **given** a term and its own parent, **then** S2 contributes and S8
  does not; **given** unrelated terms, **then** neither. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.8** *(first node of a family)* — **Given** a graph where a node's family, terms and block are
  unique to it, **when** candidates are gathered, **then** any candidate comes from S5 or S6, and the
  result may legitimately be empty. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: **Ranking and capping**

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.9** *(evidence explains the score)* — **Given** any candidate, **then** `evidence` is
  non-empty and its points sum exactly to `score`. → *property.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.10** *(cap and threshold)* — **Given** 25 scoring candidates with `max_pairs_per_node: 10`
  (the criterion fixes the number it tests; the profile default is 6, D13),
  **then** exactly 10 are returned, they are the 10 highest, ties break by node id, and the run counts
  record 15 dropped by the cap. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.11** *(determinism)* — **Given** the same graph, **when** candidates are computed twice in
  different insertion orders, **then** the results are identical, including rank order. → *property.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: **Pairs and selection**

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.12** *(pair key symmetry and sensitivity)* — **Given** nodes A and B, **then**
  `pair_key(A,B) == pair_key(B,A)`; **when** either node's text changes, **then** the key changes. →
  *property.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.13** *(no self pair, no duplicates)* — **Given** any node, **then** it is never its own
  candidate, and a pair appears at most once per run. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.14** *(which nodes are checked)* — **Given** nodes with statuses `unchecked`, `stale`,
  `validated` (unchanged) and `conflict`, **then** the first two are checked, the `validated` one is
  skipped, and the `conflict` one is checked again. → *unit.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.15** *(exhaustive mode)* — **Given** 6 checked nodes, **when** `sddc pairs --exhaustive` runs,
  **then** it returns all 15 pairs with scores, judges nothing, and makes no model call. →
  *integration.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **AC-5.16** *(counts recorded)* — **Given** a compile run, **then** the run record carries the CT-5.3
  counts and they add up: proposed = capped + dropped_below_min_score + dropped_by_cap. → *contract.*

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D1 — ⚑ Two extra candidate sources, S5 keywords and S6 same measured property**, beyond the
  pre-rel01 rule. *Why:* the old rule cannot propose the first node of a family and misses
  no-shared-term conflicts. *Rejected:* embeddings — non-deterministic, and they answer "reads alike"
  rather than "about the same thing".

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D2 — ⚑ Fixed additive scoring with a per-node cap.** *Rejected:* judging every candidate — the cost
  is unbounded; a learned ranker — no training data and no determinism.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D3 — ⚑ An exhaustive mode for measurement only.** *Why:* the design's biggest risk is a missed
  pair, and this is the only honest way to measure it.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text: - **D4 — ⚑ `pair_key` includes both text hashes**, so an edit re-opens exactly the pairs it touches.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D6 — Starting values adopted** (resolves Q1): ~~`max_pairs_per_node: 10`~~ **6 since D13**, `min_score: 1.0`,
  `min_shared_keywords: 2`, and the §4.3 weights. ⚠ They are **starting values, not findings**: the run
  counts (CT-5.3) and the exhaustive mode exist so G4 can replace them with measured ones. Changing a
  weight or a threshold is a profile change, never a code change.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D7 — `(global)` constraints are proposed only against nodes sharing a term or a keyword with them**
  (resolves Q2). *Rejected:* proposing every node — a single global constraint would otherwise flood
  every candidate set and consume the run budget.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D8 — One fixed, versioned stop-word list in code** for `keywords` (resolves Q3, and F2 Q2 for the
  same field). *Rejected:* a profile setting — two projects with different lists could not be compared,
  and the list is not the kind of thing a user should have to tune.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D9 — ⚑ A layer alone does not put a node in a constraint's scope** (M3 gate review, I-57; owner
  2026-09-19). A selector that names a family, term or category covers the nodes matching it, narrowed
  by its layers if it has any. A **layer-only** selector is a global constraint within those layers, so
  it takes D7's bar: the node must also share a term or keyword. One function serves S3 and F4's card
  (`model/scope.py`). *Why:* on R12, Q-DESC gave layer-only scopes to constraints about the checking
  process ("nodes unchanged since their last run are skipped" → L1, L4, L5). S3 then made about 60
  pairs among 43 nodes, each above `min_score` on S3 alone. With D9: 16. *Rejected:* lowering S3's weight
  below `min_score`. That would also weaken the constraints that name their scope.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D13 — ⚑ `max_pairs_per_node` is 6, not 10** (R20, from the M4 gate's data). The cap is where cost
  lives: the check phase makes one judgement per pair. On R17's store, 10 gave 184 pairs and 6 gave
  117 — **36 % fewer** — and every pair a human had judged real survived both. *Rejected:*
  `min_score: 2.5`, which cuts as much but deletes the keyword-only class entirely — the "SQLite versus
  100 concurrent writes" shape that S5 exists for (D1), and the class P3 belongs to. ⚠ Judged on one
  31-node store and four real pairs: a starting value, like the rest (D6).

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D12 — ⚑ S8: two kinds of one thing** (after R17: I-76). Q-TERM had already filed
  `export_archive` and `workspace_export` as kinds of `export` — and nothing paired the claims about
  them, because neither term is the other's ancestor. A shared parent is a weaker signal than a shared
  term and scores 1.0 against 2.0. Measured on R17's own store: the 5 GB/5 GiB pair moves from rank 63
  to **43**, at 25 more candidates (159 → 184). *Rejected:* scoring it as a full shared term — "file
  path" and "file size" are also siblings, and they are not the same subject.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D11 — ⚑ S2 follows `broader`, and S6 takes a shared keyword** (R15, after the M4 gate: I-73).
  All six planted conflicts were proposed, and five ranked 81st–130th of 137, because each side of a
  pair had been given its own term: `export_archive` against `workspace_export`, `export` against
  `nightly_backup_export`. S1 and S2 were dead on every one of them.
  *S2* now counts a term that is **a kind of** the other's (F2 D16 already records it, and nothing read
  it). *S6* now needs a shared term **or keyword**, not a shared term: two quantities of one dimension
  in claims about the same words are the shape S6 exists for. Measured on the gate's own store: the
  5 GB/5 GiB pair moves from rank 123 to **50**, the alias pair from 81 to **43**, at the cost of 19
  more candidates (137 → 156). *Rejected:* dropping S6's requirement entirely — it would pair every
  number in the corpus with every other; and raising S5's weight — it lifts noise and signal equally.
  ⚠ The two planted pairs with **no quantity** (P3, P4) are not helped by either change.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D10 — ⚑ The CT-5.3 counts count proposals, not distinct pairs** (T15). A pair both of whose ends
  are checked is proposed twice, so AC-5.16's identity
  (`proposed = capped + dropped_below_min_score + dropped_by_cap`) only holds if every number counts
  proposals. The pairs handed to F6 hold each `pair_key` once (AC-5.13). *Rejected:* counting distinct
  pairs everywhere — the identity would fail on any graph where both ends are checked, which is most of
  a first compile.

heading_path: F5 — Related-node retrieval: which pairs are worth judging
text:
- **D5 — Deferred: `checked_against` per node** (conflict-list item 5.4). A batch run checks the whole
  graph, so the cheaper `last_checked_run` plus `stale_reasons` is enough for rel01. It returns with
  incremental checking.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
**Ask the model one question about one pair at a time, turn the answers into links and conflict
records, and end the run with a report of every conflict in the spec set.**

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
This is the purpose the whole compiler serves (vision §2): finding the contradictions, duplicates and
silent overlaps that a human reading a spec set cannot reliably find. Everything before it — blocks,
atoms, layers, families, candidates — exists so that this question can be asked narrowly enough to be
answerable and cheap enough to be asked often.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
**In scope:** the Q-PAIR question and its answer schema · which answers create links and which create
conflict records · statuses and the registry · when a conflict closes · re-judging after edits · the
end-of-run report · the run budget shared with atomization.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
4.1 Where the check phase sits (rel01 D26)
text:
`sddc compile` runs: **ingest (F1) → atomize every pending block (F3) → check (F6) → report**. The check
phase starts only when atomization has finished, so every node that exists is visible to every pair.
The phase never stops early: a conflict is recorded and checking continues.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
One Q-PAIR call judges **one pair**. It receives both nodes' canonical form, verbatim text, layer,
family and source location, and it must answer with exactly one relation kind:

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: | `none` | The two claims are independent | Nothing recorded except the judgment |

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: | `refines` | A is a more specific statement of B | `refines` link A → B |

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: | `depends_on` | A presupposes B | `depends_on` link A → B |

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: | `duplicates` | Both state the same claim | `duplicates` link **and** a conflict record, kind `duplication` |

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: | `subsumes` | A already implies B | `subsumes` link; a conflict record, kind `subsumption`, **only** when the two differ in modality or in a quantity (⚑ D2) |

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: | `contradicts` | Both cannot hold | Conflict record, kind `contradiction`, and a `conflicts_with` link |

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
Every answer carries a `rationale` and a quote from each node. A quote that is not found verbatim in
that node's text fails guard G2 and is re-asked once (F3 §4.3, §4.4).

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
Conflict records are F2 CT-2.4: id, kind, sorted members, rationale, the quotes, `state`,
`detected_run`. Creating one sets `conflict_ids` on both members, which derives their status to
`conflict` (F2 §4.6), which puts them in the registry (F4 CT-4.2).

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
Two members are enough. A node in several conflicts carries several `conflict_ids` (rel01 D14), and
`sddc conflicts` groups records that share a member so interlinked conflicts are read together.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
4.4 Ambiguous nodes are judged, provisionally (⚑ D3)
text:
A node with status `ambiguous` still takes part: a vague spec can still contradict a precise one.
Verdicts involving an ambiguous node are recorded with `provisional: true`. When the ambiguity is
resolved, every provisional verdict touching that node is marked stale and re-judged.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- A pair's judgment is stored in the lock under its `pair_key` (F5 §4.4) plus the Q-PAIR schema version.
  A lock hit is replayed; no model call is made (F3 §4.7).

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- When a node's text changes, its `pair_key`s change, so every pair touching it is judged again, and
  the stale verdicts from the old text are discarded.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: - `--no-replay` forces re-asking.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: A record moves to `resolved` only when:

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: 1. the pair is judged again and the answer is `none` or a non-conflicting relation; or

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: 2. a member is deleted (F2 §4.9), with reason `member_deleted`.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
**An edit alone never closes a conflict.** Changing the text makes the verdict stale and schedules a
re-judgement; the record closes when that re-judgement says so. A `resolved` record stays in
`conflicts.jsonl` as history, with its `resolved_run`.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
Pair judging and atomization share `atomizer.max_calls_per_run` (F3 CT-3.4). The check phase reports
how many calls it used. If the budget runs out mid-phase:

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: - what has been judged is written;

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: - the remaining nodes keep status `unchecked` or `stale`;

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: - the run exits `5` and the report says checking is incomplete, naming how many pairs were left.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: Checking order is F5's order, so a resumed run continues predictably.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: At the end of a run, `compile` prints, and writes through F4:

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
```text
compiled 4 files · 37 blocks · 52 nodes · 18 terms
checked 44 pairs (31 judged, 13 replayed) · 6 model calls · 12,480 tokens
CONFLICTS: 3 open (2 contradiction, 1 duplication) in 2 groups
  CF-000001 contradiction  N-000017 sharing.md:5  ↔  N-000042 sharing.md:22
    "expires 30 days after it is created" ↔ "valid for one hour"
    rationale: both set the lifetime of a share link, to different values
  …
ATTENTION: 2 items (1 inferred_node, 1 term_unsure) — run `sddc review list`
exit 3
```

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: - Exit `3` when open conflicts exist, `0` when none, `5` when the budget stopped the phase.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: - `--json` emits the same content as one object, for scripts and for G4 measurement.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
Pairs judged, replayed, by answer kind, conflicts opened, conflicts closed and their reasons, calls and
usage. These extend the run record (CT-6.2) and are the raw material for measuring the compiler later.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: **Judging and recording**

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.1** *(contradiction opens a record)* — **Given** a candidate pair and a fake `contradicts`
  answer, **then** one conflict record exists with kind `contradiction`, both ids sorted in `members`,
  the rationale and both quotes; both nodes carry its `conflict_ids` and derive to status `conflict`;
  the registry lists both. → *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.2** *(none records nothing but the judgment)* — **Given** a fake `none` answer, **then** no
  link and no conflict record exist, and the judgment is in the lock. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.3** *(refines and depends_on make links only)* — **Given** fake `refines` and `depends_on`
  answers, **then** links of those types exist with `provenance: judgment`, a judgment id and a
  rationale, and no conflict record. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.4** *(duplication)* — **Given** a fake `duplicates` answer, **then** both a `duplicates` link
  and a conflict record of kind `duplication` exist. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.5** *(subsumption only conflicts when they differ)* — **Given** `subsumes` where both nodes
  have modality `MUST` and no differing quantity, **then** a link exists and no record; **given**
  `subsumes` where one is `MUST` and the other `SHOULD`, **then** a record of kind `subsumption` also
  exists. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.6** *(quote guard)* — **Given** an answer whose quote is not verbatim in the node, **then** the
  question is re-asked once; on a second failure no verdict is recorded and both nodes stay unchecked
  for that pair. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.7** *(direction rule)* — **Given** `contradicts` with `direction: a_to_b`, **then** the answer
  is rejected by the schema check. → *contract.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.8** *(low confidence)* — **Given** a `contradicts` answer with `confidence: low`, **then** the
  record is created **and** both nodes gain ambiguity `low_confidence_verdict`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.21** *(a criterion does not duplicate its requirement; D16)* — **Given** a `V` node whose
  `verifies` lists node B, **when** the judge answers `duplicates` or `subsumes`, **then** no conflict
  record and no link are made and the run counts one `suppressed`; **when** it answers `contradicts`,
  **then** the record is opened as usual. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.22** *(a criterion does not duplicate its own spec; D19)* — **Given** a `V` node and a
  non-`V` node from the **same file**, `verifies` empty, **when** the judge answers `duplicates` or
  `subsumes`, **then** no record and no link are made and the run counts one `suppressed`; **when** it
  answers `contradicts`, or the other node is in another file, or both are `V` nodes, **then** the
  record is opened as usual. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.23** *(one block does not duplicate itself; D19)* — **Given** two nodes with the same
  `source.block_id`, **when** the judge answers `duplicates` or `subsumes`, **then** no record and no
  link are made and the run counts one `suppressed`; **when** it answers `contradicts`, **then** the
  record is opened as usual. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.20** *(a human verdict is recorded; G4 §4, D14)* — **Given** an open conflict, **when**
  `sddc conflicts judge CF-000001 --verdict real --note "…"` runs, **then** `.sdd/adjudications.jsonl`
  gains a record naming the conflict, the verdict, the note, the members and the `judgment` it
  answered; **when** the pair is judged again, **then** that verdict reads `stale`; **given** an
  unknown conflict id, **then** exit `2`. → *unit.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: **Batch behaviour**

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.9** *(never stops)* — **Given** five candidate pairs where the second and fourth contradict,
  **then** all five are judged, two records exist, and the run continues to the end (rel01 D26). →
  *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.10** *(report lists everything)* — **Given** that run, **then** the report names both
  conflicts with their members, files and lines, groups records sharing a member, states the counts,
  and exits `3`. → *golden.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.11** *(clean run)* — **Given** a graph with no conflicts, **then** the report says so and the
  run exits `0`. → *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.12** *(budget exhausted)* — **Given** a call cap smaller than the pairs to judge, **then**
  judged verdicts are written, unjudged nodes keep `unchecked` or `stale`, the report says checking is
  incomplete with the number of remaining pairs, and the run exits `5`. → *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: **Replay, staleness and closing**

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.13** *(replay)* — **Given** a completed check and no source change, **when** the run repeats
  with a fake backend that fails on any call, **then** it succeeds with zero calls and identical
  records. → *property.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.14** *(edit re-opens the pair)* — **Given** a judged pair, **when** one node's text changes,
  **then** its `pair_key` changes, the pair is judged again, and the previous verdict is not reused. →
  *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.15** *(an edit alone does not close a conflict)* — **Given** an open contradiction, **when** one
  member's text is edited but the re-judgement still answers `contradicts`, **then** the record stays
  open with the new quotes. → *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.16** *(re-judgement closes)* — **Given** an open contradiction, **when** a re-judgement answers
  `none`, **then** the record is `resolved`, `conflict_ids` are cleared on both nodes, their status is
  re-derived, and the registry no longer lists them. → *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.17** *(member deleted closes)* — **Given** an open contradiction, **when** one member is
  deleted, **then** the record is `resolved` with reason `member_deleted` (F2 AC-2.23). → *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.18** *(ambiguous nodes are judged provisionally)* — **Given** an `ambiguous` node in a pair,
  **then** the verdict is recorded with `provisional: true`; **when** the ambiguity is resolved, **then**
  that verdict is stale and re-judged. → *integration.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **AC-6.19** *(counts)* — **Given** any check phase, **then** CT-6.2 counts are recorded and
  `pairs_judged + pairs_replayed` equals the number of candidate pairs. → *contract.*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D1 — One closed list of relation kinds, one per pair** (conflict-list item 6.3). *Rejected:* letting
  the model return several relations — the compiler could not act on a mixture, and it invites
  hedging.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D2 — ⚑ `subsumes` opens a conflict only when the two differ in modality or quantity.** Plain
  subsumption is useful structure, not a defect; a `MUST` subsumed by a `SHOULD` is a defect. Made
  configurable because this is a judgement call to revisit with real data.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D3 — ⚑ Ambiguous nodes are judged, with `provisional` verdicts** (item 6.5). *Rejected:* skipping
  them — vague specs are exactly where contradictions hide; accepting their verdicts as final — the
  claim may change when the ambiguity is cleared.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D4 — A conflict closes only on re-judgement or member deletion** (item 6.4). *Rejected:* closing on
  text change — it would report "fixed" for an edit that changed nothing relevant.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D5 — ⚑ One run budget shared with atomization**, and exit `5` with an explicit "incomplete" report
  rather than silently checking less (conflict-list item X.1).

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D6 — ⚑ `confidence: low` records the verdict and flags the nodes**, rather than dropping it.
  *Rejected:* discarding low-confidence verdicts — a silent miss is worse than a flagged guess.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D7 — Deterministic checking order** (item 6.7). Which conflict is found first is then reproducible.
  Whether a *fixing* order changes the final graph is a property to measure in G4, not a claim here.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text: *None. Q1–Q3 were resolved 2026-09-18 as D8–D10 (rel01 D28).*

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D8 — The pair question carries the two nodes plus their layer and family labels, and nothing else**
  (resolves Q1). *Rejected for rel01:* including refinement ancestors or the constraints covering each
  node — it grows every prompt for a benefit nobody has measured. If verdicts look uninformed on a real
  corpus, this is the first thing to change, and the judgment lock makes the before/after comparable.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D9 — One conflict list, sorted with contradictions first**, then duplications, then subsumptions
  (resolves Q2). *Rejected:* a separate hygiene list — it splits the reader's attention and invites
  ignoring one of the two lists. Sorting solves the "40 duplicates bury 3 contradictions" problem
  without hiding anything. The counts per kind are in the report header, so a large duplication count is
  visible at a glance.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D16 — ⚑ A criterion never duplicates or subsumes what it verifies — checked in code** (R17,
  I-77). D15 says it in the prompt and the judge opened CF-000002 for exactly that case, so the graph
  settles it: when one node's `verifies` holds the other's id (resolved from the criterion's own
  citation, F2 D13), a `duplicates` or `subsumes` verdict records nothing and is counted as
  `suppressed` (CT-6.2). A **contradiction** between a test and its rule is still reported: a test that
  denies its requirement is a real defect. *Why in code:* a prompt rule is a request, and this one was
  refused; `verifies` is a fact the graph already holds.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D18 — ⚑ Q-PAIR is batched: 8 pairs per call** (R21; rel01 D30's lever, applied to the phase that
  now dominates a compile). §4.2 said "one Q-PAIR call judges one pair", and the M4 gate showed what
  that costs: 159 calls for 159 pairs, $2.35 on 28 blocks, and ≈ $55–70 extrapolated to this
  repository (I-75). A headless call carries ≈ 22k tokens of harness prompt whatever it asks, so the
  call count *is* the cost. **The condition F3 §4.3 rule 4 puts on batching holds here too:** each
  pair's answer is validated on its own, and a failure re-asks **that pair alone**. With D13's cap,
  the same corpus needs **15 calls instead of 159**. *Rejected:* a larger batch — Q-DESC settled on 8
  (rel01 S21) because a longer call risks the timeout, and a timeout costs the whole batch.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D19 — ⚑ The document's form settles two more non-conflicts, in code** (I-81, after the dogfood).
  D16 fires only when a criterion cites its rule, and on this repository's own specs most criteria
  cite nothing: precision there was ≈ 10 %, and 65 of 70 conflicts involved a criterion or a decision
  entry. Two facts the graph already holds now settle a `duplicates` or `subsumes` verdict the same
  way D16 does — nothing recorded, counted as `suppressed` (CT-6.2):
  (a) **a criterion and a claim of its own spec file** — exactly one of the two is a `V` node and both
  come from one file; a criterion restates its spec's rules by design;
  (b) **two claims of one block** — the same `source.block_id`, as a decision entry's heading and
  its body are.
  **A contradiction is never suppressed by either**: all four real finds of the dogfood were
  contradictions, one between a criterion and its own spec (CF-000038), one between two sentences of
  one paragraph (CF-000001). Measured on the dogfood store before building: (a) removes 22 of the 70
  records and (b) 5, none of them among the four real. *Given up:* a criterion that genuinely
  duplicates prose of its own file is no longer reported; duplication **across** files, and between
  two criteria, still is. *Rejected:* suppressing contradictions between criteria describing different
  situations by label — CF-000038 is in that class; that one needs the judge to see the situation,
  not a rule on the layout.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D17 — ⚑ The judge is shown the terms, and how they relate** (after R17: I-76). Retrieval delivered
  the 5 GB / 5 GiB pair and the judge answered `none` — *"the two claims govern different export types
  (export archive vs workspace export)"* — while the graph held both as kinds of `export`. Each claim
  now lists its terms, the question states how the two sets relate (same term, a kind of, or two kinds
  of one thing), and the instructions say a different name is not a different object. *Rejected:*
  renaming nodes' text to a canonical term — the verbatim span is the evidence a person checks.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D15 — ⚑ Q-PAIR is told when two numbers are *not* a contradiction** (R16, after the M4 gate:
  I-74). Eight of eleven reported conflicts were false, and five were one mistake: a 24-hour link
  inside a 30-day archive, a 13-day restore inside a 14-day window, read as contradictions — and once
  the judge computed "day 30 versus day 31", arithmetic the text does not do. The prompt now states
  that two claims contradict only if both must hold for the same thing at the same time, gives the
  three consistent shapes (a limit inside a longer one, a window and what follows it, a rule and its
  clarification), forbids calculating, and says that an acceptance criterion restating its requirement
  is design, not duplication. *Rejected:* a code-side numeric check — the relation between two
  quantities is exactly the judgement the model is asked for.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D14 — ⚑ An adjudication answers one model verdict, not a conflict id** (T19, G4 §4). The record
  keeps the `judgment` it answered and the members at the time, so a pair judged again marks the human
  verdict **stale** instead of carrying it forward — the person answered about the old text. Records
  are appended, never rewritten, so a change of mind stays visible and M2 can be recounted at any time.
  *Rejected:* a `human_verdict` field on the conflict record — it would be overwritten by the next
  re-judgement, which is exactly the history M2 needs.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D13 — ⚑ A node the check phase looked at loses the stale reasons that scheduled it** (T17), and
  records the run in `last_checked_run`. *Why:* `stale` means "needs re-checking" (F2 §4.6); keeping the
  reason after the re-check would leave the node stale for ever and re-judge it every run. The reason
  is still written by whatever caused it — a deleted neighbour, an edited counterpart — so a node is
  never silently dropped from the queue; it is discharged only by the phase that honours it.
  *Rejected:* clearing it when the graph is written, which would discharge reasons nobody acted on.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D12 — ⚑ CT-6.2 also counts what was *not* judged** (T17): `candidates` (how many pairs retrieval
  proposed), `unjudged_failed` (answers that failed their checks twice), `provisional` (§4.4), and F5's
  own `retrieval` counts. *Why:* AC-6.19's identity reads "judged + replayed = candidate pairs", and a
  pair that failed twice would otherwise break it silently — the I-59 lesson, that a zero with no
  reason is a failure the report must show.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D11 — ⚑ The direction rule is in the schema, not in a later check** (T16). CT-6.1 says `none`,
  `duplicates` and `contradicts` are symmetric; the JSON Schema now says so too (`if`/`then`), so
  AC-6.7's answer is rejected before anything reads it, and the re-ask carries the reason. *Rejected:*
  silently normalising the direction to `symmetric` — that would hide a judge that did not understand
  the question.

heading_path: F6 — Conflict detection: judge the pairs, record the conflicts, report them all
text:
- **D10 — `confidence` is recorded and flagged, never acted on** (resolves Q3). rel01 stores it and
  raises ambiguity `low_confidence_verdict`; nothing filters or re-ranks by it until G4 has compared it

> **Status:** Living · **Adopted:** 2026-09-17 · **Tier:** authoritative, release-independent.
> **Read this first.** [`constitution.md`](constitution.md) says *how* to build; this says *what* is
> being built and *why*.
> **Audience:** the owner, and any AI agent proposing, designing or reviewing work here.
> **Previous vision:** scrapped 2026-09-14, frozen at
> [`../archive/2026-09-13_vision_pre-rel01.md`](../archive/2026-09-13_vision_pre-rel01.md). Nothing in
> it binds unless re-adopted here.

**A compiler for specifications: it turns a set of Markdown spec files into a checked graph of
atomic specs, and reports where those specs contradict, duplicate or under-specify each other.**

Spec-driven development lets people describe a system in ordinary language, which is its whole
advantage and the source of its problem: English has no type checker. Two specs written weeks apart
can contradict each other and nothing notices. The larger the spec set, the less likely a human — or
an AI agent reading it — will notice either.

The SDD Compiler reads the prose, breaks it into atomic claims, places each one in a layered graph,
and checks the claims against each other. **The prose stays the source of truth; the graph is a build
artifact**, the way object files are downstream of source code.

| **1** | **Make a spec set checkable.** Find the contradictions, duplicates and ambiguities a human reading cannot reliably find. | Conflicts found in a real spec set that a human review had missed, and the false ones it raises |

| **2** | **Make a spec set usable by an AI coding agent.** Give an agent the few specs that govern the change it is making, instead of a folder to read. | Whether an agent's output honours the specs it was given — designed later (rel01 G4) |
Purpose 1 comes first: an agent cannot be helped by a spec set nobody has checked.

- **O1 · The prose is the source of truth.** The graph is compiled from Markdown files and can always
  be rebuilt from them. Nobody edits the graph by hand.

- **O2 · The compiler's code is deterministic.** Structure, identity, placement, storage, comparison
  and status bookkeeping are plain code. Given the same inputs and the same recorded judgments, a
  build produces identical bytes.

- **O3 · Language judgment belongs to a model, in small closed questions.** The model answers narrow,
  schema-bound questions — "what claims are in this paragraph?", "do these two contradict?" — never
  open ones. Every answer is checked by code before it is accepted, and recorded so a rebuild replays
  it instead of asking again.

- **O4 · Fail loud, and never invent.** A model answer that cannot be anchored in the source is
  refused or flagged, never silently kept. Every conflict carries its quotes and its reasoning.

- **O5 · Two forms of one graph.** A collapsed form for humans and a full-detail form for AI agents,
  both derived from the same records, so they cannot disagree.

| Input | **Several static Markdown spec files**, compiled in one batch run. Hardest shape supported: a spec tree like this repository's own `sdd/` | Live specs typed at the CLI; specs written during an AI session |
| Trigger | One command, run by a person | Editor and agent hooks; compile on save |

| Conflicts | Detected across the whole set, **recorded and reported together at the end of the run** | Immediate feedback while specs are being written; an agent that fixes its own conflict before continuing |
| Model | Haiku through headless Claude Code (default) or the Anthropic API | Local models as assistants |
| Output | The graph, a conflict report, and generated human views | Context packs for code generation; an interactive viewer |
| Code generation | Designed, not built | Built |
| Versioning, multi-author, design-vs-as-built comparison | Out | In |

**rel01 in one sentence:** *point it at a folder of spec files, and get back a graph plus a list of
every conflict in it.*

- **No new specification language.** Authors keep writing ordinary Markdown. Structure is inferred,
  never demanded.
- **No editing of specs by the compiler.** It reports; people and their agents decide and rewrite.

- **No arithmetic or bookkeeping inside a model prompt.** Offsets, quantities, counts and statuses
  are computed by code.
- **No hidden model output.** Nothing enters the graph without a quote from the source.

- **No graph as source of truth.** If the graph and the prose disagree, the prose wins and the graph
  is rebuilt.
| Lecture — explanation, alternatives, background | HTML in `docs/lectures/` | Never |
| Working design, specs, decisions | Markdown | Specs: yes · design: once adopted |
If a lecture and a Markdown file disagree, **the Markdown wins**.

- **Proposing or designing?** Start here, then `../design/rel01_brainstorm.md`. Work that serves no
  purpose in §2, or contradicts §3 or §5, is out of scope — say so rather than building it.

- **Implementing?** This file binds nothing directly. Go to [`constitution.md`](constitution.md) and
  the governing spec.

- **Amending?** The purposes (§2), principles (§3) and non-goals (§5) change only when the owner says
  so, and the change lands here first. The release scope (§4) is expected to churn.
